chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us, from Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal, from his father. He said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever recalls our tragedy and weeps for what was committed against us will be with us in our rank on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever is reminded of our tragedy, weeps, and makes others weep, his eye will not weep on the Day that the eyes will weep. And whoever sits in a gathering in which our affair is revived, his heart will not die on the Day that the hearts will die.

key_terms.أبكى: Makes others weep — the act of moving others to tears through narrating the Ahlulbayt's suffering
key_terms.مصابنا: Our tragedy — referring to the sufferings of the Ahlulbayt, particularly the events of Karbala
key_terms.يحيى فيه أمرنا: Revives our affair therein — keeping alive the cause and memory of the Ahlulbayt through gatherings (majalis)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the rewards for mourning the Ahlulbayt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) describes three spiritual rewards for those who mourn the Ahlulbayt: sharing their rank on the Day of Resurrection, immunity from weeping when all eyes weep, and preservation of one's heart from spiritual death. This hadith, narrated in a Ramadan gathering in 367 AH, emphasizes that mourning rituals (majalis) are not merely emotional displays but acts of spiritual solidarity with the Imams that carry eschatological rewards.
